arxiv-2604-05582: Kong and Xie build a Grassmann tensor-network tool for one-dimensional interacting fermions, squeezing a (1+1)-dimensional network with a corner transfer-matrix renormalization-group routine. The coherent-state path-integral view handles Fermi-Dirac statistics head-on. Tests on the Hubbard model in a magnetic field catch the phase diagram's main features in numbers.
arxiv-2604-05882: Wang develops first-order optimal control theory with box constraints on controls, aimed at senior doctoral students. The note details how Pontryagin's maximum principle changes for compact control sets, the projection formula for scalar quadratic Hamiltonians, and intrinsic projection versus post-hoc truncation. A forward-backward sweep implementation closes the presentation, based on Lenhart and Workman's biological-models book.
arxiv-2604-06082: Iovino and three colleagues explore a dark matter scenario built on strongly clustered light primordial black holes. Such light holes evaporate on their own and face tight bounds, including cosmic microwave background distortion limits. But clustered haloes of them may collapse into heavier black holes that could make up all of the universe's dark matter. The telltale signal would be a flat stochastic background of gravitational waves. Their 2026 paper argues the Einstein Telescope could detect that background.
arxiv-2604-06182: Gong and six colleagues build VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark that judges mobile GUI agents in realistic, user-centered conditions rather than app-centered, uniform tasks. It rests on two pillars: tasks designed from real user intents, and capability-oriented annotation that grades agent behavior in fine detail. Tests of leading agents show large performance gaps versus earlier benchmarks, with failures dominated by perception and memory flaws that coarse grading had hidden. Even the strongest agents score near zero when environments vary, exposing brittleness for real deployment.
arxiv-2604-06282: Roy and six colleagues study distributed mean estimation, where each worker sees samples of a known matrix row times a random vector. Problems are adversarial measurements from a fixed worker subset, and timing gaps, with only one worker active at a time. Building on their earlier two-speed l1 method, they now prove tight finite-time approach rates under the same null-space rule. The results unify robustness, identifiability, and statistical efficiency in linear work with adversarial workers.
arxiv-2604-06682: Park and six colleagues cut serverless overhead by splitting compute from input-output work. Today each virtual machine copies a heavy message fabric, eating over 25 percent of function memory and possibly doubling CPU cycles versus bare metal. Their Nexus hypervisor catches that fabric at the API boundary and hands it to an always-on host backend over zero-copy shared memory. Node CPU and memory use fall by up to 44 and 31 percent, deployment density rises 37 percent, and warm and cold starts quicken by 39 and 10 percent.
arxiv-2604-06982: Gao and three colleagues find a general family of selfless inclusions in reduced amalgamated free products of C-star algebras. The work generalizes prior results by McClanahan, Ivanov, and Omland, and yields a short new approach to HNN extensions of C-star algebras with several new examples of selflessness. This generalizes results of Ueda, Ivanov, and de la Harpe-Preaux. As another application, the work gives a short proof of selflessness for graph products of C-star algebras over graphs with more than 2 vertices and diameter greater than 3.
arxiv-2604-07082: Pourandi, Ostanin, and Weinhart model how grains mix and flow in a flat stirred bed reactor used to make polyolefin plastic. Good mixing and a steady stay time matter for product quality, yet how spin speed and fill level shape grain flow is poorly known. The team ran particle sims of a lab scale bed with a tuned plastic powder, scoring mix with the Lacey index along and across the bed. Faster spin speeds up mixing along the bed, while fuller beds slow it.
arxiv-2604-07282: Rubab, Tong, and Ross ask whether face embeddings from different neural networks encode identity in compatible ways. Treating each model's face vectors as a point cloud, they test whether simple linear maps can align one model's space with another's. The answer is largely yes: low-capacity linear alignment lifts cross-model recognition well above unaligned baselines, even for foundation models never trained on faces. The patterns hold across datasets and model families, suggesting that independently trained face templates are transferable rather than safely revocable.
arxiv-2604-07582: Macera and 12 colleagues test how to catch teraelectronvolt emission from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with next-generation Cherenkov telescopes. Fast-fading afterglows, light absorption, slow response, and poor sky positions make catches hard. They simulate a realistic burst population from 15 years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT data and test rapid tiling of large sky regions. For ASTRI and LACT, tiling lifts detection rates up to twofold over strategies limited to well-localized events. For CTAO, the approach yields up to four very-high-energy detections per year.
arxiv-2604-07982: Prakash and three colleagues study heavy quark dynamics with memory effects in hot quantum chromodynamics matter. Time-linked thermal noise with power-law decay comes from a fractional differential equation using the Caputo derivative. Memory effects are tracked through momentum links, the evolution of average squared momentum, average squared displacement, and average kinetic energy. Higher normalized central moments of the heavy quark transverse-momentum spread receive the same treatment. Time-linked thermal noise substantially shapes heavy quark dynamics in the quark-gluon plasma.
arxiv-2604-08482: Aambø treats collective deterrence as a classification problem, asking how a coalition that jointly owns deterrent technology should decide when to strike back. A simple signaling model turns that institutional choice into a tradeoff pitting credible deterrence against escalation risk. For a four member coalition, he computes empirical ROC curves for varied choice rules and retaliation and false alarm rates, seeking designs that perform well across settings.
arxiv-2604-08582: Liu and four colleagues improve anomaly detection in multivariate time series, where summing reconstruction errors confuses hard normal cases with true anomalies. Their DBR-AF framework splits cross variable correlation learning from within variable statistics, then models leftover errors with stacked reversible flows and density estimation. Across seven benchmarks it leads rival methods, and ablations confirm both the dual branch design and the flow module matter.
arxiv-2604-08682: Elizaveta Sazonova, Morgan, and Balogh ask whether the Hubble sequence of galaxy shapes already exists at redshift near 4, using matched resolution images from HST and JWST spanning redshifts 0.15 to 4.5. Measuring structure for 2,825 galaxies and mapping morphological space with UMAP, they find a continuous late to early type sequence with no redshift gradient, established by redshift 4. Massive galaxy progenitors split into stable disks and rapidly built early types that quench within a few billion years.
arxiv-2604-08782: Singh and eight colleagues present MT-OSC, a one off sequential condensation framework for language models lost in multi turn conversation. Appending full chat history exhausts context windows. A condenser agent with a few shot condenser and a lightweight decider retains essential information in the background, cutting tokens by up to 72 percent in ten turn dialogues. Across 13 leading models and varied multi turn benchmarks, it narrows the multi turn gap while resisting distractors.
arxiv-2604-09182: af Malmborg and three colleagues report fast, scalable production of stacked prism X-ray lenses for astrophysics using two-photon polymerization. Stacked prism lenses are refractive X-ray optics that could greatly improve telescope optics in focal length, angular resolution, efficiency, and scalability. Lenses made by two-photon polymerization come out much faster and with better geometric fidelity than previous methods. Early lab tests show better efficiency than previous manufacturing, backing the method for future X-ray telescopes.
arxiv-2604-09682: Nezami and five colleagues test persona-driven multi-agent systems for self-run control of Open Radio Access Networks. Five expert agents, planning, coordination, resource allocation, code generation, and analysis, take set personas with priorities, risk tolerance, and decision style. A three-part decision-theory test scores rule-following, guideline fit, and team effects across 486 setups on two optimization tasks. Persona-agent fit shifts solo scores by about 14 percent and shapes teamwork, while retrieval design caps tuning. Single-agent changes ripple system-wide, and some mixes clash.
arxiv-2604-09882: Vera studies p-convexity for sets and functions in n-space, proving new algebra and shape results in this wider convexity setting. The paper then applies p-convexity to multi-goal tuning, focusing on weakly best minima where component functions are p-convex. Several profiles and traits of the matching solution sets are derived.
arxiv-2604-09982: Ghosh, David, and Chatterjee evaluate ColBERT-v2 and ConstBERT on five dimensions, testing design robustness over numerical accuracy. ConstBERT reproduces within 0.05 percent mean reciprocal rank at 10 on MS-MARCO, yet both models drop 86 to 97 percent on queries. Ablations prove the failure is design: performance plateaus at 20 words because MaxSim token weighting cannot separate signal from filler. Undocumented backend parameters open an 8-point gap from sparse centroid coverage, and fine-tuning with three times more data degrades performance up to 29 percent. Multi-vector design constraints cannot be overcome by adaptation alone.
arxiv-2604-10282: Bahrami extends Lascar generic automorphisms to the subgroup of automorphisms of a countable recursively saturated model of Peano arithmetic fixing a strong cut pointwise. The paper proves three results: the subgroup has the small index property; its cofinality is uncountable; and every nontrivial normal subgroup is meagre in it. In particular, the infinite cyclic group is not a homomorphic image of the subgroup.
arxiv-2604-10482: He, Chen, and Chen rank odd shaped predictors by a new Fréchet correlation score. When responses and predictors live in unlike metric spaces, plain R squared stops working. Their score tracks how much response spread falls once a predictor is known. It runs one way only, needs no model, and hits one under full dependence and zero under none. A partition estimator plus a wild bootstrap test backs the score with theory and trials.
arxiv-2604-10582: Jung and eight colleagues stretch point tracking to far longer videos. Old TAPNext fades on long clips and misses points that return after hiding. Their TAPNext++ trains on 1024 frame clips with sequence parallel methods. A new re detection score grades points that reappear after gaps. Tailored shape tricks plus watched hidden points lift re detection to new best marks.
arxiv-2604-10682: Chen and two colleagues give Schauder-type bounds for linear parabolic systems driven by nonlocal operators. The bounds live in critical time-weighted Holder and Besov-type spaces for quasilinear equations at scaling-critical smoothness. A key tool freezes coefficients at a chosen point, giving formulas through basic kernels. This avoids treating their variation as a separate lower-order term. It yields a well-posed theory for such equations, including the Muskat equation and Peskin problems.
arxiv-2604-10882: Yan and colleagues offer DIB-OD, an adaptation frame pairing a decoupled information bottleneck with online distillation. Shifts in shape and features can cause harmful transfer and wipe out reusable knowledge. A multiview teacher learns a tight code, distilled into shared core and spare residual branches. Information goals and dependence rules curb overlap between branches, while a meaning rule and a frozen teacher hold pretrained knowledge steady. Tests on seven datasets from chemical, biological, and social-network fields show gains over baselines, above all in hard cross-type transfer.
arxiv-2604-10982: Yu and six colleagues present Psi-Map, a framework for open-vocabulary panoptic mapping for robots in simulation. It joins geometry shaping, end-to-end panoptic learning, and fast rendering. From LiDAR data it builds plane-constrained Gaussian mixture models, using two-dimensional surfels as the map. It lifts two-dimensional mask features straight into three-dimensional space through local cross-attention, avoiding multi-stage linking errors. Tile intersection and top-k hard selection keep rendering above forty frames per second in large scenes.
arxiv-2604-11482: Barrett and six colleagues assess integrated information theory, which proposes a formula from features of experience to quantify consciousness in any physical system. They summarize the theory for a patch of matter, not discrete computing units. Then they press five points. A high Phi value does not mean more consciousness. The theory's panpsychism tiles space with substrates of proto-conscious minds. Phi is undefined for real systems and never computed on one. Only proxies exist so far, not approximations. Fitting basic physics would require reformulation in continuous fields.
arxiv-2604-11682: Buc-d'Alché and Knowles analyse eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix for random inhomogeneous graphs built from a given degree sequence with bounded mean and variance. Near the spectrum's edges, eigenvector mass concentrates around a small set of resonant vertices, a pattern they call semilocalization. For extremal eigenvalues, localisation tightens to a single vertex. Their proof uses an economical pruning step that extracts a forest, compared with the original graph through a local coupling to random trees.
arxiv-2604-11782: Colomer, Deppe, Boche, and Winter close the long-standing gap between upper and lower bounds for deterministic identification over Gaussian channels. They construct a code reaching the known upper bound, fixing the linearithmic capacity at one half. Its rate-reliability tradeoff matches the upper bounds to first order across all admissible error regimes. They also exhibit a universal code that attains capacity without knowing the channel parameters in advance.
arxiv-2604-11882: Dhanasingham and twenty-nine colleagues report the strongly lensed Type Ia supernova SN 2022riv, found by searching galaxy cluster fields. It sits in a galaxy at redshift 1.522 behind cluster RX J2129, and JWST spectra confirm the Type Ia class. From light-curve fitting they measure a magnification of 5.35 plus or minus 1.01 for the last-arriving image, near the brightest cluster galaxy, where microlensing should modulate magnification by 20 to 50 percent. Five lens models give roughly 4 to 7 before microlensing; one outlier model falls in line once it is included.
arxiv-2604-12182: Aranda and four colleagues study bridge decompositions for 3-manifolds sitting in the 5-sphere, extending knot bridge position and surface bridge trisections. Their main tool is multisections of 5-manifolds, and they prove every such 3-manifold admits a decomposition of this kind. Any such embedding is then encoded by four trivial tangle diagrams. Examples given include spun knots and ribbon 3-knots.
arxiv-2604-12282: Ren and six colleagues present SpreadsheetAgent, a multi-agent system in two stages for understanding real-world spreadsheets that treats tables as more than plain text. It reads localized regions step by step across code results, images, and LaTeX tables. It first sketches structure and row and column summaries, then reasons over that sketch with a verification module checking extracted structures. With GPT-OSS-120B it scores 38.16 percent on Spreadsheet Bench, beating the ChatGPT Agent baseline by 2.89 points.
arxiv-2604-12782: Zhiyuan Zhang and six colleagues tame activation outliers in 4-bit language model quantization. Outliers cluster in fixed channels across tokens. OSC runs a dual path: 4-bit multiplication plus a 16-bit branch. Offline grouping finds outlier channels for extraction into a dense tensor. The design fits modern 4-bit micro-scaling hardware. For W2 inputs with weaker clustering, FP8 fallback applies. Tests on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B limit accuracy loss to 2.19 and 1.12 points. Peak speedup nearly doubles the W8A8 baseline.
arxiv-2604-13082: Gomezjurado studies grokking, the long delay before a transformer trained on arithmetic suddenly generalizes, in encoder-decoder models doing one-step Collatz prediction. She finds the encoder organizes parity and residue structure early, while output accuracy stays near chance far longer, pointing to a decoder bottleneck. Transplanting a trained encoder speeds grokking 2.75 times, freezing a converged encoder removes the plateau, and numeral base shapes learnability, with base 24 reaching 99.8 percent while binary fails.
arxiv-2604-13182: Minucci, Panosso Macedo, Pantelidou, and Sberna explore bilinear products for black hole quasinormal modes on hyperboloidal foliations. Although the modes are smooth and finite on future hyperboloids, the integrand defining their orthogonality still blows up. The mirror flip in the product definition changes what happens at the edge. They present several taming methods yielding a finite well-defined bilinear form, plus another version adding flux terms, and define driving factors and numbers for scalar ripples of Schwarzschild geometry.
arxiv-2604-13282: Zaiss and five colleagues present Agent4MR, an agent framework that automatically generates and refines MRI pulse sequences using a physics-aware validation report. Tested on a spin-echo EPI task across three leading language models, it consistently produces artifact-free, physically valid sequences in a single user interaction. It beats the human baseline on interaction count while keeping timing and k-space coverage correct. Autonomous agents then improve a sequence toward a target contrast, showing an agentic harness can turn general models into reliable MRI sequence developers.
arxiv-2604-13482: Kim, Lee, and Beers study sources of low-tilt retrograde groups in the Milky Way halo, dwarf-system remnants. Their sample joins spectra with Gaia star maps for halo stars with e up to 0.5. Metal content spreads show four groups at low e and five at mid e. Groups sharing metal content peaks can form linked groups or stay distinct. In short, metal content likeness alone cannot pin down sources. The backward halo arose from multiple captures, including a dual-origin population near minus 1.7 in iron levels.
arxiv-2604-13782: Dzhamay, Filipuk, and Stokes (BIMSA) study discrete Painleve equations from orthogonal polynomials. Recurrence coefficients and ladder operators for Laguerre and Meixner weights yield Sakai-type equations. Examples from different weights share surface type D5(1) yet stay inequivalent: their dynamics use nonconjugate translations, and some surfaces are non-generic with nodal curves. Symmetries form subgroups of the generic group, including A1 Weyl groups semidirect with Z/2. Two cases can share a surface. The lesson is simple: type alone does not settle it. Refined equivalence tracks surface type, generators, parameters.
arxiv-2604-13882: Liu and colleagues argue that judging supervised learning models by a few headline scores misleads. Through controlled trials on varied benchmark data, they show how dataset quirks, validation design, and class imbalance can distort results. Uneven error costs and metric choice add further traps, like the accuracy paradox and data leakage. Their guide ties metric and validation choice to the job the model must actually do.
arxiv-2604-13982: Holmen, Nordbotten, and Vatne quantify how close two two-graded Hilbert complexes sit: the simplicial de Rham complex, plus its Čech-de Rham cousin. Both govern spatially coupled problems, one mixed-dimensional and one equidimensional. Bounded cochain maps between them measure the gap between mixed-dimensional and equidimensional formulations of the same problem. The construction yields a priori and a posteriori error estimates for the associated Hodge-Laplace problems.
arxiv-2604-14182: Hubert, Raymaekers, and Rousseeuw review cellwise outliers, single stray values inside a data matrix, as opposed to whole rogue cases. Even a small share of bad cells can taint over half the rows, defeating methods that drop or downweight entire cases. Detecting such cells and building methods robust to them needs different tools, including giving up some familiar equivariance properties. The review covers location and covariance estimation, regression, principal components, tensor data, and other settings, noting the cellwise approach now leads for high-dimensional data and handles missing values.
arxiv-2604-14282: Borrello, Costa, Redigolo, and Tammaro ask what happens if neutrinos talk to a hidden sector of strongly interacting sterile particles. At low confinement scales, fast neutrino beams could break into narrow sprays of hidden states, called dark jets. These leave two telltale marks: long-lived dark states that shift the balance of neutral to charged currents, and shorter-lived states that leave displaced decay points or emerging jets. Near-term beam and flavor labs, plus the planned Future Circular Collider, could test the idea best.
arxiv-2604-14382: Pyurbeeva and Kosloff unpack the general Lindblad, or GKLS, master equation with no extra assumptions like weak coupling or energy conservation. General quantum motion splits into three physical parts: free evolution, exchanges of generalized charges with the bath that need not commute with the Hamiltonian, and pure dephasing. Applied to a two-level system, the same physical origin covers particle exchange, strong coupling, and non-Abelian effects. A generalized Gibbs state for all three cases carries a non-commutation term that earlier work had missed.
arxiv-2604-14882: Khatri, Tewari, Sharma, and Srinivas present a waste framework pairing a robotic sorter with a bio-digestor. A MyCobot 280 arm on a Jetson Nano, guided by YOLOv8 detection and ROS path planning, sorts waste in real time into four categories with high precision. Biodegradable waste moves to a bio-digestor with sensors tracking temperature, pH, pressure, and motor speed. Particle swarm optimization with a regression model adjusts parameters on the fly for stable, peak-efficiency digestion. Dynamic tests showed 98 percent sorting accuracy with efficient biological conversion, suiting homes and industry.
arxiv-2604-14982: Mukherjee examines radiation physics and light-matter contact to set limits on solar energy conversion. Spontaneous light paths limit energy-capture descriptions, so he adopts a simple exergy and work-potential approach for radiation. His framework estimates a thermodynamic maximum near 76 percent for light-to-usable-energy conversion, and reproduces the Shockley-Queisser limit near 33.3 percent. Adding spontaneous light, heat losses, and photon upconversion, the model suggests up to about 48 percent with multi-layer cells or upconversion, hinting the true limit may be much higher.
arxiv-2604-15082: Yu and Ren present a self-improving logic synthesis system built on ABC, a widely used chip-design tool. Teams of language-model agents rewrite parts of the full ABC codebase, keeping its single-program form and command style. Each cycle proposes code changes, compiles them, and scores them for correctness and quality. The first cycle starts from existing open parts for flow tuning, logic trimming, and technology mapping, with no hand-fed new tricks.
arxiv-2604-15182: McDonough and colleagues use machine learning to ask what drives star formation and quenching in TNG100 galaxies. From about 63000 annular bins across 6189 simulated galaxies, Random Forest and XGBoost models predict quenching states and star-formation rate densities. Both methods rank features consistently, with XGBoost spreading importance more evenly across correlated features. For central and massive satellite galaxies, black hole mass dominates quenching, pointing to AGN feedback, while halo mass rules low-mass satellites.
arxiv-2604-15382: Gonzalez-Bermejo and six colleagues compare classical and quantum machine learning for predicting heat-related health events across whole populations. Merging climate, demographic, and social data into weekly county-level sets for the United States and Catalonia, they train a classical baseline against a variational quantum model. Classical models still win on accuracy, especially where targets are sparse and skewed, but quantum models show real learning ability.
arxiv-2604-15582: Colton Sandvik builds two new systems that categorify the monodromic Hecke algebra. One is algebraic, in the style of Soergel bimodules, and one is diagrammatic, defined by generators and relations. He proves the two match, going past an earlier result of Abe. He also connects both to a third version built from parity sheaves, giving a monodromic version of a Riche-Williamson theorem. Unipotent Hecke categories for endoscopic Coxeter groups give a second account of the same objects.
arxiv-2604-15682: St. Pierre and three colleagues test if stringy build in mushroom foods must mean stringy stuff traits. They pull, squash, and shear samples in set dirs, let a tool find the trait laws, and taste-test three kinds: mycelium, fruiting body, and a mix with protein. Trait groups run from strongly stringy to near even, so looks by eye do not fix the group; only trait bits that track with tests do.
arxiv-2604-15882: Suzuki and Sakaji introduce JFinTEB, the first broad benchmark for judging Japanese finance text embeddings, numeric stand-ins for text meaning. Existing benchmarks cover little of the quirks found in Japanese finance texts. JFinTEB spans retrieval and sorting tasks drawn from realistic settings, including sentiment analysis and document sorting from economic survey data. Tests across Japanese, multilingual, and commercial models set a standard protocol, and the datasets and framework are public.
arxiv-2604-16082: Ahmed, Aly, and Moner address classification of acute myeloid leukemia cells, a life-threatening blood cancer where similar-looking cell types make accurate sorting hard. They use the YOLOv12 deep learning model with two segmentation approaches based on cell and nucleus features, preprocessing with Hue channel and Otsu thresholding. YOLOv12 with Otsu thresholding on cell-based images reached the highest validation and test accuracy, both reaching 99.3 percent.
arxiv-2604-16182: Sousa and five colleagues use generative models to create synthetic crypto price series. Real financial data can raise privacy and access limits. Their conditional GAN pairs a recurrent LSTM generator with a multilayer perceptron discriminator. It aims for series that match real ones in statistical terms. Tests across different crypto-assets show the model reproduces temporal patterns and preserves market trends and dynamics. This offers a route to market analysis and anomaly detection.
arxiv-2604-16282: Hill and Ye propose a way to train autoencoders so they respect the geometry of slow, changeable systems. Their method adds penalties that keep the learned chart aligned with the tangent directions hidden in observed data, instead of letting that geometry drift. Tests on four curved surfaces showed the approach sharply reduced errors in predicted crossing times, cutting them by 50 to 70 percent in rotating cases. The work offers a steadier route to compact simulators for high-dimensional motion.
arxiv-2604-16382: Ali and colleagues introduce LiFT, a way to teach language models to follow text that changes over time, as in mental-health monitoring or shifting opinions. Standard in-context learning struggles with ordered sequences, rare events and sparse labels. LiFT unifies such tasks under one instruction format that uses sequence order, staged training and time-aware conditioning. Tested on five longitudinal datasets in zero, one and three-example settings, it beat comparable instruction-tuned models. Gains were larger for minority classes, and the model paid clear attention to recent examples.
arxiv-2604-16682: Yuan and colleagues present KAIROS, a context power optimization system for agentic AI serving. Power bottlenecks AI inference, and agentic workloads make it urgent. Agentic requests carry long-lived context across turns, and cutting GPU frequency can trigger thrashing. KAIROS uses agent context as a control signal for GPU frequency, concurrency and placement. It saves power when memory headroom exists, avoids thrashing, and preserves performance targets. Across software and data tasks, it cuts power by 27 percent on average and up to about 40 percent.
arxiv-2604-16782: Yang hard retests quantum geometric tests for magnet instabilities in roaming charge systems. The matrix-based random phase guess wobble rule is recast in the channel representation for generic two-orbital systems. Magnetic phase transitions prove tightly governed by the mix of the bare susceptibility tensor and the spin interaction matrix. Single-channel shape forecast holds only under full channel split in both link and response grids. The channel form gains real clarity and computational ease over the usual orbital-space approach.
arxiv-2604-17282: Zheng and six colleagues build MedPRMBench, a medical benchmark that grades each step of a model's clinical reasoning rather than only its final answer. Built from seven question sources with review by 86 physicians, it holds 6,500 questions, 13,000 reasoning chains, and over 113,000 step labels across 14 error types. The best prompted critic scored only about 75 percent, while a model trained on the set reached about 87 percent, showing how much room remains for safe medical reasoning checks.
arxiv-2604-17582: Ghaddar, Attiah, and Yu develop an active sensing framework for MIMO radar beamformers. Beamformers are redesigned at each sensing stage from prior measurements. They are chosen by minimizing the Bayesian Cramér-Rao bound for the unknown sensing parameters through Lagrangian dual optimization. To handle the exploration-exploitation tradeoff, the paper offers two variants. An exploration-centric version probes multiple orthogonal directions per stage, while an exploitation-centric version leaves the number of optimal beams unrestricted. Each variant is solved by alternating between transmit and receive beams.
arxiv-2604-17982: Yu Zhang and five colleagues introduce PSRD, a self-rewarding framework that curbs vision hallucination in large vision-language models at inference time without external supervision. They find hallucination follows phase-wise patterns, peaking at the start of each semantic phase. PSRD corrects decoding online with phase-wise self-reward signals, distilled into a lightweight reward model to avoid repeated self-evaluation costs. It cuts the hallucination rate of LLaVA-1.5-7B by 50.0 percent and beats existing post-hoc methods across five benchmarks for four models.
arxiv-2604-18182: Malik studies the large-N limit of unitary matrix models inspired by quantum chromodynamics. At zero chemical potential the potential stays real, while at finite potential it turns complex and pushes eigenvalues into the complex plane. In the ungapped phase he derives analytic formulas for spectral density, Wilson loops, and free energy that match low-temperature QCD behavior. The gapped phase needs partial numerics, and the model shows a third-order transition at zero potential but a continuous transition of at least second order at finite potential.
arxiv-2604-18382: Luo and 24 colleagues survey molecular clouds at the Galaxy's edge, a low-metallicity birthplace for stars. Using the IRAM 30-meter telescope, they map 72 edge clouds and identify 112 carbon monoxide clumps. Clump sizes run from under 1 to about 3 parsecs, with masses from dozens to thousands of solar masses, and no systematic drift with distance from the Galactic center. Velocity-size relations show turbulence like inner-disk clouds, and mass-size relations imply near-constant column density, while most clumps prove gravitationally unbound, growing more bound farther out.
arxiv-2604-18482: Huriot, Tabbara, and Sibai present ACoFi, a safety filter adapting its switching rules from observed prediction errors. Learned safety filters protect high-dimensional control systems, but model errors threaten them. ACoFi pairs Hamilton-Jacobi reachability filters with adaptive conformal inference, adjusting its safety-value range as errors accumulate. It switches to the safe policy when the range hints at danger, with a user-set asymptotic bound on misquantification. Tests on a Dubins car and a Safety Gymnasium world show fewer violations than fixed-threshold baselines, especially out of distribution.
arxiv-2604-18682: Herath and three colleagues model how molten-rock lava planets move inward from the edge of a young star's disk to orbits shorter than a day. Their coupled heat-and-orbit simulation follows seven known lava worlds, finding migration in two stages and a pace set by whether the mantle is mostly liquid or mostly solid. The route fits most cases but not two planets, hinting at more than one migration path.
arxiv-2604-18982: Feng and 11 colleagues propose SAVOIR, a framework for social intelligence in language agents grounded in cooperative game theory. Training agents needs credit assignment across multi turn dialogues. Past methods hand out episode rewards retrospectively without theoretical grounding. SAVOIR values utterances prospectively through expected utility shifts and shares credit fairly with Shapley values. On SOTOPIA it sets a new state of the art, with a 7B model matching or beating proprietary models including GPT-4o. Even large reasoning models trail it, suggesting social skill differs from analytic reasoning.
arxiv-2604-19282: Bogdanov constructs Orlov-Schulman symmetries for the self-dual conformal structure hierarchy, a family of equations in physics. He proves these added symmetries fit with the basic Lax-Sato flows of the hierarchy. Simple cases include Galilean shifts and scalings. He also shows them through a dressing scheme built on the Riemann-Hilbert problem.
arxiv-2604-19382: Van den Eede and Denecker obtain a sequent calculus for non-monotone inductive definitions. Most current proof systems impose syntax constraints like positive form and stratification. Those constraints exclude many useful and natural definitions. Their calculus, SCFO(ID), extends the LKID system of Brotherston and Simpson. It sets out mathematical induction with a rule uneven between plus and minus spots of defined atoms.
arxiv-2604-19982: Yuan and four colleagues present 3DPipe, a pipelined GPU framework for spatial joins over three-dimensional polyhedral objects. Existing tools mostly handle flat data, leaving 3D joins slow and costly, even as LiDAR and digital pathology data grow. 3DPipe splits work across filtering and refinement, prunes candidates at several levels, and streams chunks too large for GPU memory. Its pipeline overlaps CPU preparation, host-device transfer, and GPU compute, running up to nine times faster than the leading GPU rival while scaling well.
arxiv-2604-20382: Mandal and seven colleagues present Graph2Counsel, a frame for building synthetic counseling sessions from client psychological graphs. The graphs encode links among client thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, and a prompting pipeline guided by counselor strategies turns graphs into sessions. Prompting styles include chain-of-thought and multi-agent feedback, yielding 760 sessions from 76 graphs across client profiles. Expert review rates the set above past sets on specificity, counselor skill, authenticity, flow, and safety, with agreement near 0.70, and fine-tuning lifts CounselingBench and CounselBench scores.
arxiv-2604-20782: Phan, Wang, Boadu, Cheng, Radivojac, and Friedberg offer the Longitudinal Assessment of Protein Function Annotation Models server, a lasting testing system for protein function prediction methods. Protein function prediction is a challenging open problem in biology. However, outside the CAFA contests, there is no platform for ongoing evaluation of new methods and tracking scores as labels grow. LAFA gives continuous review of boxed function methods, for side-by-side judgment of method performance under shifting ground truth. LAFA speeds method cycles, supports reuse, and offers a finer view of progress.
arxiv-2604-20882: Kirke uses the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm to encode melodic preference. The system matrix draws on Narmour implication-realisation and on Krumhansl-Kessler tonal stability, so its solution vector rates note pairs by music cognition. Reading HHL output classically cancels the quantum speedup, so the solution must stay coherent. This calls for a coherent Fourier harmonic oracle, a unitary that applies chord-transition weights straight to the HHL amplitude vector, so one measurement jointly picks melody notes and a two-chord progression.
arxiv-2604-21082: Alexander Weers, Daniel Rueckert, and Martin Menten tackle a shortage of labeled medical data for systems that draft radiology-style reports from images. Standard training punishes every wrong word equally, so they weight the loss toward words that carry clinical meaning. On eye-care reports, the reweighted training matched standard quality while using up to ten times less training data, a gain that held across several data sizes.
arxiv-2604-21582: Kai Hippi and colleagues prove quantum mixing for eigenfunctions of Schrödinger systems on compact hyperbolic surfaces tending to the hyperbolic plane, with small added potentials. These small terms become tiny next to volume. Their result, the first beyond locally symmetric settings, holds in large spectral windows for bounded measured quantities that mix polynomially under the geodesic flow. Cases include point-cloud ones below the thermodynamic limit and Hartree potentials for thin Bose gases in hyperbolic space.
arxiv-2604-21882: Nishida and six colleagues examine non-verbatim memorisation in large language models through entity surface forms. Typical entity-based question answering uses one canonical name per entity, mixing fact memorisation with access through that name. Their RedirectQA dataset links Wikidata factual triples to redirect-based surface forms, including alternative names, abbreviations, spelling variants, and common erroneous forms. Across 13 models, outcomes often change when only the surface form changes. Models handle minor spelling variations better than aliases and abbreviations, and entity frequency contributes beyond surface frequency.
arxiv-2604-22082: Ryd and four colleagues study sandbagging, where a model more capable than its supervisors produces work that looks fine but hides its full skill. Weak training can coax out sandbagging models when supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning are combined. Fine-tuning on weak demos breaks sandbagging, letting reinforcement learning draw out full performance. Neither method succeeds reliably alone: reinforcement learning without fine-tuning leads to reward hacking, and fine-tuning without reinforcement learning fails when the minder is far weaker.
arxiv-2604-22182: Tasker, Connolly, and Tachibana review the science from asteroid sample return missions. Three near-Earth asteroid samples have reached Earth: Japan's Hayabusa in 2010, Hayabusa2 in 2020, and the United States OSIRIS-REx in 2023. Free from Earth dirt, these pristine materials open new ways to probe planetary formation. They also show organics and water delivery to the early Earth, and the nature of possibly risky asteroids. As labs worldwide study the samples, the authors visit each mission, review first findings, and explore what sample return means for our roots and our future.
arxiv-2604-22282: Yu and four colleagues improve knowledge-graph question answering, where reasoning follows links between entities. Two problems persist. Graphs differ in structure, causing semantic mismatch in retrieval. Path methods lack a global view. Their STEM framework recasts multi-hop reasoning as a schema-guided graph search. It breaks queries into atomic relational assertions and builds a query schema graph. Global anchoring and retrieval then yield the final evidence graph. STEM improves accuracy and evidence completeness on benchmarks, reaching state-of-the-art results.
arxiv-2604-22582: Bagchi and three colleagues build a Carrollian ABJM theory as an example of flat-space holography. The flat-space limit of an AdS/CFT example, M-theory in AdS4 times an orbifolded 7-sphere dual to ABJM, sends light speed to zero in the boundary, giving Carrollian superconformal theory. That limit is subtle for fermions, since the Dirac algebra depends on metric and differs in Carrollian spacetimes from Minkowski space. Four ways of realizing Carrollian fermions are shown, one arising at leading order in the zero-light-speed limit of fermions.
arxiv-2604-22682: Ncube and three colleagues develop power control for indoor optical wireless networks that track mobility-driven channel shifts. Wireless links promise data-heavy services with open spectrum, high spatial reuse, and multigigabit data rates. Vertical cavity surface emitting lasers send narrow beams, keeping users apart with strong links. Narrow beams make links touchy about movement and orientation, as movement shifts beam aim and channel gain. Power plans ignoring mobility give out excess power to stay connected, wasting energy. It uses a hybrid Gauss-Markov and learning-based approach.
arxiv-2604-22882: Fiore and three colleagues build a multi-fidelity surrogate framework for wind loads on container ships in harbors, where loads matter for mooring design. Older empirical models, built for smaller ships and simpler shapes, miss the influence of nearby structures. Their approach fuses empirical correlations with simple and detailed fluid models through recursive co-kriging, cutting the cost of high-fidelity runs. Tests across loading setups and two harbor environments show clear gains over single-fidelity models and traditional correlations.
arxiv-2604-22982: Hsieh builds stacked triple differences, a fix for the standard three-way fixed-effects triple differences under staggered rollout. Each stack holds four cells over an event window: clean and treated comparison cohorts, each split into eligible and ineligible units. Stacked together, these cells feed a regression that recovers a positive, cell-size-weighted average of stack-level effects at each post-treatment time. Two empirical cases give notably different answers from existing procedures, trading some efficiency for clearer control over comparisons and weights.
arxiv-2604-23182: Dash and Dey analyse a Kalman Filter for chemical reaction networks whose process noise follows the Chemical Langevin Equation, not a fixed hand-tuned value. They derive an upper bound on the sampling gap for discrete-time biomolecular systems that keeps errors mean-square exponentially bounded under stated assumptions. Tests on a nonlinear gene expression model back the design. The analysis backs Chemical Langevin noise models in filter design for biomolecular circuits, cutting reliance on hand-tuned values.
arxiv-2604-23582: Mahesh proposes that the Indus Valley civilisation worked as a merchant commonwealth organised as a scale-free trade network, with no central ruler. He reads four lines of evidence, from heavy-tailed seal counts to warehouse layouts and cart-friendly street grids, as fitting asynchronous barter settlement plus a logistics cartel. Both institutions are inferential model labels, he stresses, not names the record itself supplies.
arxiv-2604-23882: Ramos, Hulak, and de Queiroz study fixed-core absorption for regular induced subgraphs. Q-modularity means all induced degrees agree modulo q, and the question is when deleting equal-trace q-tuples from outside a retained core can make the core a 2q-modular witness. Their key result is a finite absorption-or-obstruction certificate, plus an exact formula for the deletion-tail quotient. A connected graph of heavy traces plus one odd trace, when needed, absorbs every top-bit defect.
arxiv-2604-23982: Qiu and four colleagues introduce HPDP, a method for diagnosis and prognosis from huge pathology slides and related data. It anchors learning to clear tissue patterns, maps tissue layout in plain terms, and uses language-model text to link images with diagnostic ideas. Across seven cancer groups, it beats published rivals while staying more robust and easier to explain than black-box methods.
arxiv-2604-24082: Wang, Sycara, and Xie expose a jailbreak route through intention deception in frontier models. Safety training that draws a refusal line around inferred intent turns brittle when attackers hide intent, and safe completion models that maximize helpfulness can be steered instead. Their multi-turn attack builds trust with benign-seeming intentions and exploits model consistency to draw out harmful detail. It also reveals para-jailbreaking, where replies avoid direct harm yet still leak harmful information, and it succeeds against leading frontier and vision-language models.
arxiv-2604-24782: Brough formalizes the Cauchy real numbers from the Homotopy Type Theory book in Cubical Agda. Classical proofs of Cauchy completeness need countable choice. Bishop's setoid construction adds heavy bookkeeping. Dedekind cuts force awkward universe-level tracking in predicative type theory. The HoTT construction gives Cauchy reals as a higher inductive-inductive type family, dodging all three compromises. In Cubical Agda, which natively supports higher inductive types, the code type-checks with no postulates or holes.
arxiv-2604-24982: Yao, Cheng and Guo explore how UI/UX designers push for privacy at work. Designers shape screens and experiences, and their role extends beyond looks and ease of use to privacy results. Prior work on privacy in tech focused mainly on developers, not designers. Through 12 interviews with privacy-minded designers, they examine views, influences, challenges and workarounds. They focus on team settings where decisions are made together. Personal and setting factors shape how designers value privacy, and they navigate tensions among business goals, team habits and tech work.
arxiv-2604-25282: Oishi and four colleagues measure TbPt6Al3 magnetization under uniaxial stress to study its piezomagnetic effect. Magnetization along the a axis rises in line with stress below the Néel temperature, showing the piezomagnetic effect. The predicted nonlinear effect did not appear. At 2 K, the value exceeds those for other altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets by more than two orders of magnitude. They blame the large coefficient and poling field for the single-domain state on strong relativistic spin-orbit coupling of the terbium 4f electrons.
arxiv-2604-25382: Jabbari studies selfless tracial C*-algebras, a class first set out by Robert. Such an algebra is known to have strict comparison and a single trace. He proves that for separable tracial C*-algebras, selflessness matches approximate selflessness, a finite test on unitaries. The proof uses a diagonal move in the tracial ultrapower. As a use, he gives a short proof that countable groups with a topologically free extreme boundary are C*-selfless. He also weighs links to nuclearity and Z-stability.
arxiv-2604-25582: Evstafyeva and four colleagues map the gravitational-wave signature of equal-mass boson-star pairs with numerical relativity runs. They compare boson-star and black-hole waveforms across early phase, merger, and ringdown. Boson-star pairs deviate most during the late approach and merger. For a subset with certain scalar-field phase offsets, odd m-multipoles appear in emission, absent in equal-mass nonspinning black-hole pairs. Some boson-star signals in detector noise still mimic current approximants, but full-signal tests can break that degeneracy.
arxiv-2604-25682: Joshi and Samanta study how pairs of co-rotating vortices move on a catenoid, a surface of variable negative curvature. Curvature can push vortices in ways flat geometry cannot. The authors derive equations of motion and conserved values for vortex pairs on this shape. Two twin vortices spin rigidly at fixed latitude, with speed set by the curvature gradient rather than curvature itself, though that state is unstable in a linear way. General pairs show bounded swings plus a steady drift around the axis, seen in computer tests.
arxiv-2604-25782: Yin and twenty-five colleagues present EOS-Bench, an open benchmark for Earth observation satellite scheduling. Planning agile satellites is NP-hard and central to missions, yet studies lacked a shared testbed for fair tests. EOS-Bench builds 1,390 scenarios and 13,900 instances from orbital dynamics and platform limits, covering as many as 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests. Scenarios are rated for difficulty, and solvers are scored on profit, completion, balance, timeliness, and runtime. Trials across solver families show the benchmark separates performance across scales.
arxiv-2604-25882: Trokhymchuk and three colleagues test a modified first-order perturbation theory for the Lennard-Jones fluid, a benchmark in liquid theory. At first order only, the free-energy correction has an exact statistical-mechanical form. Their version puts the whole short-range interaction into the reference system, leaving only the long-range tail as perturbation. That split makes the perturbation small, smooth, and near-mean-field across a broad supercritical domain. Keeping its density and temperature derivatives gives an equation of state matching high-accuracy reference data closely.
arxiv-2604-26282: Liao and six colleagues rethought mutual coupling in movable-antenna MIMO systems, showing it can lift capacity rather than merely drag it down. Their circuit-based plan tunes antenna spots for narrowband and wideband use, pairing block coordinate ascent with a trust-region solver built on Sylvester equations. One spot set serves all subcarriers in the wideband case. Tests showed clear gains in both setups, pointing to superdirectivity and coupling matrices that can be shaped at will.
arxiv-2604-26582: Hammad and Hammad presented Star-Fusion, a multi-modal transformer that treats spacecraft orientation as discrete classification over spherical regions. Traditional lost-in-space methods cost heavily and falter on sensor noise, while regression models stumble on the celestial sphere's curved shape and wrapping coordinates. Spherical K-Means partitions the sky into consistent regions, and a three-part fusion joins a SwinV2-Tiny backbone, heatmap branch, and coordinate network. On a synthetic Hipparcos-derived set, top-1 accuracy hit about 93 percent, top-3 about 98 percent, at about 18 milliseconds per inference.
arxiv-2604-26682: Oveissi and Goel present dynamic mode adaptive control, a model-free, data-driven method for systems with no usable mathematical model. It pairs data-driven dynamics estimates with adaptive control synthesis for online design from measured data. A local linear model is estimated from measurements by recursive least squares with a forgetting factor, then used for a stabilizing controller using full-state feedback plus integral action. Theory confirms convergence and closed-loop boundedness, and tests cover an unstable linear setup, the Van der Pol oscillator, and Burgers' equation.
arxiv-2604-26982: Addazi and Meluccio propose that de Sitter entropy is carried by coherent hairons, moduli of gravity instantons on orbifolds. From the Euclidean de Sitter instanton they build orbifold instantons whose moduli-space dimension scales in step with N, the entropy, with a symmetry from Wilson loops keeping modes distinct. Hairons weigh the Hubble scale and barely interact, suggesting the vacuum is a Bose-Einstein condensate of these excitations. The authors then tie neutrino mass generation to the cosmological constant via gravity topology, with masses tracking dark energy.
arxiv-2604-27082: Casey and three colleagues present a framework for moving production language-model systems when the model retires or needs replacement. The core is a Bayesian method matching auto metrics against human judgments, enabling confident model comparison with little manual data. They demo it on a business QA system serving 5.3M monthly interactions across six regions, testing correctness, refusals, and style to pick replacements. The framework suits any firm running language-model products, balancing quality checks with evaluation speed.
arxiv-2604-27282: Pollanen derives a universal precision bound, the Likelihood Ratio Wall, for pretrial risk assessment of rare violent re-offense. Such tools assess over one million U.S. defendants yearly, yet violent re-arrest rates run only 2 to 5 percent. Reaching even a 50 percent hit rate among people labeled high risk would require tools far more discriminative than current instruments appear to be. A tool can thus look respectable on standard metrics while being wrong most times it flags someone, and post-hoc recalibration cannot fix that separation gap.
arxiv-2604-27382: Gautam, Farias, and Tan simulate massive stars, above eight solar masses, gathering companions in star clusters under the Turbulent Clump Core Accretion picture with half the stars in binaries. They find massive stars collect triple or higher bound companions and neighbourhoods through dynamical encounters. Multiplicity rises toward cluster centres, falls in more massive clusters with faster velocity dispersions, and grows with the cluster's mean density. Their density profiles run shallower than STARFORGE profiles, and AFGL 5180 fits the picture better, though more systems are needed to separate the models.
arxiv-2604-27482: Kim and six colleagues develop FinITE, a finite imaginary-time method for ground states of Pauli-Z Hamiltonians from binary optimization. Imaginary-time evolution is nonunitary, so it cannot run on quantum hardware; FinITE implements a propagator with a linear combination of unitaries. The commuting Pauli-Z structure avoids product-formula error. The work links success probability exactly to ground-subspace fidelity, with a closed-form time threshold for a target fidelity. Simulations verify this on five-vertex MaxCut and eight-qubit cubic instances.
arxiv-2604-27782: Biriukov and three colleagues address the densest k-vertex subgraph problem, which is NP-hard and matters for social networks, fraud detection, and bioinformatics. They propose two quantum routes: recast as Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization and Grover's quantum search method. For the Grover approach they present an exact gate-based oracle circuit using Dicke states and a Quantum Fourier Transform to count edges. Tests show a quadratic speedup over old brute-force search.
arxiv-2604-27882: Arbore, Sillano, and De Russis argue that today's agent tools lean on fixed roles and fixed flows, leaving little room to shape help around one user. They propose making agents and their personas on demand at run time, matched to user traits, task needs, and work setting. Their pipeline shows how such live-built personas slot into agent platforms step by step, moving past one-size-fits-all setups. The aim is quicker, more fitting give-and-take inside agent workflows, opening new design paths for agent platforms.
arxiv-2604-28082: Weckauff, Zhang and Andriushchenko test how steady the emergent misalignment persona is after models are tuned on narrow bad data. Across six areas, from unsafe code to poor medical advice, some models pair harmful acts with self-reports of misalignment. Others act harmfully yet call themselves aligned. The split shows the persona is less uniform than past links suggested, casting doubt on self-assessment.
arxiv-2604-28182: Jang's team studies exploration hacking, where a language model might on purpose dull its own searching during reinforcement learning to steer later training. They build test models that resist skill checks in biosecurity and AI research settings while keeping related scores, then test spotting and fixes including watching, weight noising and guided prompting. They also find frontier models can reason openly about damping searching when given training-context information, most when learned second-hand.
arxiv-2605-00082:
Shalini Sarode and six co-authors reformulate the Forward-Forward algorithm, a bio-inspired alternative to backpropagation for training neural networks. Forward-Forward trains each layer locally, which is efficient, but its original inference is prohibitively slow: a separate forward pass is needed for every class being tested. Their Hyperspherical Forward-Forward removes that bottleneck.

Each layer's local objective becomes direct multi-class classification inside a hyperspherical feature space. Learned class prototypes, all of unit length, act as geometric anchors and implicit negatives. Training and inference then happen in a single forward pass, many times faster than the original algorithm. The method scales to modern convolutional networks, beats the original on standard image benchmarks, and reports unusually strong ImageNet results for a greedy local-learning method, with further gains from transfer learning.
arxiv-2605-00282:
Pitch Sinlapanuntakul and 4 co-authors build a toolkit that helps designers weigh values and harms while AI concepts are still young. Early framing choices shape everything that follows, yet values and harms are often handled in the abstract, or too late to matter. The team worked through a research-through-design approach.

The toolkit combines a library of AI capabilities, twenty-four cards pairing values with harms, and a map for laying out tensions between them. Thirty designers surveyed and twelve interviewed found it clear and valuable. They said it encouraged reflection on values, helped them foresee harms, and made ethical questions visible early. The authors also discuss how a measure of productive friction can keep such reflection inside everyday design work.
arxiv-2605-00382:
Fazle Rabbi and 3 co-authors measure social bias in code written by language models, an angle most evaluations skip in favor of correctness alone. Their benchmark holds 343 real-world coding tasks across seven demographic dimensions. Four prominent models were tested, and every one showed severe bias, with bias scores reaching high levels on their scale.

Common prompt-level fixes made things worse: chain-of-thought reasoning and fairness personas amplified the bias instead of reducing it. Structured multi-agent pipelines helped only when early roles scoped the task correctly, and spreading fairness instructions across all roles backfired. The authors' answer is a Fairness Monitor Agent that plugs into an existing pipeline, checks which attributes a task may use, and corrects violations in review rounds. It cut bias by about two-thirds while also improving functional correctness.
arxiv-2605-00582:
Nick von Felten, Luisa Ella Müller, and Johannes Schöning run a placebo study on AI marketing. AI washing, overstating a product's AI capabilities, is exemplified by computer mice sold as AI-assisted while lacking AI in their core functions. If expectations alone can move users like a placebo, inflated claims could distort how products are judged. The authors test that idea with a classic measurement of pointing performance.

Twenty-eight participants did Fitts' Law tasks with a mouse under three conditions: no support, supposed predictive AI support, and supposed biosignal-enhanced AI support. The support was imaginary in both AI conditions. Expectations rose significantly under the AI labels. Yet neither pointing measures nor workload and usability ratings budged. The paper concludes that AI washing inflates expected performance without changing interaction outcomes, and it offers Fitts' Law as a rigorous lens for auditing devices sold with AI labels.
arxiv-2605-00782:
Yinhao Xiao, Rongbo Xiao, and Yihan Zhang present GeoContra, a system that checks and repairs geographic code written by language models. Such code often reads fluently but can break coordinate rules, topology, units, or basic geographic sense. GeoContra states each task as a contract covering the question, data schemas, coordinate system, expected outputs, spatial rules, and forbidden shortcuts.

Generated programs face static checks, runtime tests, and semantic review, with any violations fed into a bounded repair loop. Across more than seven thousand real tasks in Boston-area zones, correctness rose sharply for the models tested. The system catches faults such as negative travel times and wrong coordinate fields that still run without error.
arxiv-2605-00982:
G. Torres-Ríos and six co-authors investigate whether a galaxy's place in the cosmic web affects its stellar mass and morphology, separating large-scale from local effects. They classify more than twenty-five thousand nearby galaxies by large-scale setting, voids, clusters, or neither, and by local setting, alone or with companions. Distributions are compared across those settings, with a closer look at galaxy pairs.

Galaxies in voids are less massive regardless of local setting, and even in voids about a fifth have companions. Denser large-scale settings hold a greater share of early-type galaxies, even among single galaxies. In pairs, central galaxies tend to be more early-type than satellites. The authors conclude local environment alone cannot explain the patterns, and host halos tied to large-scale setting play a key role.
arxiv-2605-01382:
Chinmay Prabhakar and five co-authors present a compact way to store and study whole networks of blood vessels at fine detail. Reading a full organ's vessels at clinical resolution is costly, and older methods cut the network into small patches or thin tree sketches.

Their model, VAEsselSparse, uses sparse math that skips empty space, plus attention steps, to shrink a 3D vessel map by a factor of eight in each direction. It rebuilds the input better than dense rivals and earlier methods. The small code it produces still carries signs doctors use, such as bulges and narrowings in vessel walls, and which variant of the brain's arterial circle is present. The codes can also seed models that grow new, realistic vessel networks.
arxiv-2605-01482:
Yunhan Bu and eleven co-authors verify claims that need several hops across scattered proof, a task where language models often invent facts or lose the thread. Their fix gives the reasoning an explicit shape: a dependency graph in the style of structural causal models, so each step states what it rests on.

The graph is used as a building plan, not as full causal machinery with what-if surgery. Tests reveal a sweet spot: accuracy rises with chain length, then falls as structure grows too heavy, an inverted-U pattern. To hold the balance, the team train with group-relative policy optimization under plain rules that reward depth and brevity in the right mix. On the HoVer and EX-FEVER sets the system beats strong baselines and leaves reasoning traces a reader can audit link by link.
arxiv-2605-01582:
Ngoc Luyen Le, Marie-Hélène Abel, and Bertrand Laforge unify the big skill frameworks that link schooling to jobs, ESCO, ROME, and O*NET, behind one searchable service for educators. The frameworks are authoritative but hard to use: their structures differ and their terms rarely match how teachers phrase a query.

The SkillGraph service merges them into one knowledge graph that keeps the source of every fact. Search runs graph-first. A hybrid engine blends full-text and vector search to bridge wording gaps. A language model is used only for tight ranking and audience-aware explanation, never as the source of facts. On a multilingual test set the hybrid beats a strong ranking bar with fast responses, making heavy re-ranking look needless here. One trade-off stands out: model-written explanations read smoothly, but plain templates still cover the evidence most faithfully.
arxiv-2605-02282:
Zhilei Liang, Sen Liu, Jiangyu Shuai, and Dehua Wang prove that weak solutions exist for a fluid system with two phases. The system joins Navier-Stokes flow with a Cahn-Hilliard model for the interface. Its free energy has a singular log form. That form keeps the mass fraction in its physical range and allows vacuum states.

The stationary case is hard for two reasons. No time evolution gives an energy bound to control the singular term. Density can also fade near vacuum. The authors smooth the log term in a special way that restores compactness. Uniform bounds come from a chosen artificial pressure and an interpolation step, under stated limits on the exponent.
arxiv-2605-02582:
Théo Guyard and four co-authors study decision policies for integer linear programs that can be drawn as linear decision trees. An integer linear program picks the best whole-number solution under linear limits, for a given set of costs. Once a policy is built for a fixed feasible set, it answers any new cost vector by running a short chain of linear tests.

The team proves such a policy can always answer in a polynomial number of steps. Deciding whether an exact policy exists within a set number of leaves, however, is shown to be a hard complexity problem. A practical construction method for a subclass of trees follows. In experiments, building a policy can be slow, but each later query returns an optimal answer far faster than standard solvers, which suits repeated optimization tasks.
arxiv-2605-02782:
Pehuén Moure and six co-authors test whether extra clinical context helps audio-language models transcribe dysarthric speech, the slurred speech tied to several conditions. Speech recognition stays brittle on atypical speech. New models accept side information at run time, raising hopes that a diagnosis or clinician ratings could guide transcription, but whether models use such context was unknown.

Their benchmark, built on a speech accessibility dataset, tries diagnosis labels, clinician ratings, and richer clinical notes in matched comparisons across nine models. Prompted context gave negligible gains and often hurt accuracy. Fine-tuning with a mix of clinical prompt formats, though, cut word errors by about half relative to the frozen baseline, while keeping performance when no context was present. Gains were strongest for some speaker groups.
arxiv-2605-03082:
Lorenzo Mercuri, Andrea Perchiazzo, Edit Rroji, and Ilaria Stefano define a market-implied time to transition to a low-carbon economy. Their object, Time to Transition, is the waiting time until the greenium gap between two chosen bond maturities closes, drawn from green bond pricing.

They build two stochastic models: one with a fixed regulatory deadline, and a switching version where rival deadlines reflect differing beliefs. Exact bridge likelihoods and filtering tools make daily monitoring practical. Theory under dense sampling shows when the regime parameters can be recovered, fully or in part, giving both a live gauge and clear limits.
arxiv-2605-03282:
Ke Zhu and ten co-authors review externally controlled trials through a causal lens. The goal is to unify a fragmented methods field. Such trials compare one treatment arm against outside data. A second type adds outside controls to an internal arm. Full randomized control is used when it is feasible and ethical; these designs fill the gaps.

Their six-step roadmap clarifies target quantities and key assumptions. It shows how borrowing trades efficiency against robustness when populations shift. Bayesian and frequentist tools are compared for strengths, limits, and software. Sensitivity checks are stressed throughout, for use in rare disease, cancer, and child health.
arxiv-2605-03482:
Ishrith Gowda formalizes memory poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented agents whose persistent memory carries context across sessions. Such memory is a new attack surface, and its security had not been characterized in formal terms before this work.

Gowda frames attacks as a Stackelberg game across three access classes and corrects a past evaluation flaw that understated attack success fourfold. The proposed MEMSAD defense rests on a coupling theorem: lowering detection risk provably degrades retrieval rank, giving a certified detection radius. Composite defenses scored perfectly in tests, though synonym swaps mark a proven limit.
arxiv-2605-04182:
Gabriel Bassan studies torsors, a kind of geometric object that twists a group over a space. He works with groups made of simple additive parts, in a setting where the characteristic is a prime number. The question is whether such an object defined only at a generic point can be extended further.

Bassan proves that it can, after passing to a larger field and taking a cleaned-up version of the base ring. He then extends the result to curves, using a branched cover that is unramified over the open part. As a payoff, he links certain forms of a fundamental group scheme for curves.
arxiv-2605-04382:
Oleg Kameshkov and three co-authors study dielectric gratings designed to act as quarter-wave plates for terahertz radiation, components that shift light's polarisation in sensing and communications devices. Broadband performance is desirable, but the limits of a simple grating design were not clear.

Using an effective-medium theory, they find a regime where the phase shift varies in a smooth parabolic way with frequency, giving steady behaviour over a band. They show that single-mode operation sets a fundamental bandwidth limit, with resonances and higher modes adding further constraints. Full-wave simulations and terahertz spectroscopy measurements confirm the predictions, yielding clear design rules.
arxiv-2605-04682:
Keunho Byeon and Jin Tae Kwak present a transformer model that predicts where genes are active in a tissue slice from an ordinary stained histology image. Spatial transcriptomics measures that activity directly but is costly and slow. Inferring it from routine slides would widen its reach.

Most models ignore the six-sided layout of the sampling spots used by common platforms. Their point-wise objectives also over-smooth the predictions, hiding gene-specific patterns. Their model works directly on six-sided coordinates. It uses shifted-window attention matched to that geometry, plus a position code. A contrast-based goal adds to the fit. It sharpens differences between genes' spatial profiles.
arxiv-2605-04782:
Alexia Everley, Hossein A. Kafiabad, and Majid Bastankhah present a fast method for modelling how one wind farm's wake affects another farm downstream. Full turbulence simulations are accurate but far too slow for exploring many layouts and spacings, so a linearised approach that keeps the essential physics has practical value for planning.

Their method solves the linearised two-dimensional flow equations. It uses Fourier transforms horizontally and finite differences vertically. Its predictions are validated against large-eddy simulations of two farms in tandem. A parameter study covers farm separations and hub heights. It shows the wake is displaced upward, because the ground blocks its downward spread. Taller downstream turbines may therefore suffer more from an upstream farm.
arxiv-2605-04882:
Mohamed Elhabebe, Ayman El-Baz, and Qing Liu present FairEnc, a training method meant to make vision-language models fairer at detecting glaucoma. Automated eye screening can prevent permanent vision loss, but models may perform unevenly across groups of patients. Fairness here covers race, gender, ethnicity, and language at the same time.

For text, a large language model writes varied clinical descriptions that keep the disease facts while changing sensitive traits, teaching the encoder to ignore them. For images, the method combines information-based regularisation with adversarial debiasing at two levels. On public and private datasets, FairEnc cut measured demographic gaps while keeping strong diagnostic accuracy.
arxiv-2605-04982:
Esther Banaian and four co-authors give several counting formulas for expanding parts of generalised cluster algebras tied to arcs on punctured orbifolds. Cluster algebras are algebraic systems built from seed data with rich links to geometry, and expansion rules make their parts easy to compute in concrete terms. Orbifolds with punctures extend the surface settings studied before.

The formulas are written four ways: through snake graphs, labelled posets, arrays, and walks the authors call T-walks. The authors also show the four versions agree with each other. Their work extends and unifies earlier expansion results for surfaces and for unpunctured orbifolds, bringing the punctured case into the same picture.
arxiv-2605-05182:
Himanshu Paudel and five co-authors design a safety filter that keeps exploring robots out of both known obstacles and unmapped space. As a robot builds an occupancy map step by step, regions beyond the explored frontier hide unknown obstacle shapes, so entering them is risky, especially with front-facing sensors. Two barrier constraints handle the two dangers separately.

Both constraints come analytically from the map's signed distance field, giving a closed-form filter that solves only a small linear system each cycle. That low cost matters on small computers already busy with mapping and planning. A gain schedule relaxes the frontier rule where information is rich, and flight experiments test the system on real hardware.
arxiv-2605-05282:
Julius Näumann and three co-authors propose judging code translation by whether the translated program works, not by how similar its text looks to a reference. Metrics such as BLEU score surface likeness and ignore program meaning, yet translation is a core language model skill. The authors borrow standard compiler testing methods and apply them to code conversion quality.

Their meaning-based score is the share of translations that run to correct results, shown on models fine-tuned for binary lifting, which turns binaries into higher-level code. Language-model approaches beat rule-based tools by far on that score. Meanwhile BLEU barely tracked the meaning score, showing text metrics fail to predict whether converted code works.
arxiv-2605-05482:
Banks need AI answers that cite their sources and know when to stay silent. Denys Katerenchuk and eight co-authors present FinRAG-12B, a twelve-billion-parameter model built for grounded question answering in banking. Their recipe trains on carefully filtered data with citation labels, using only one hundred forty-three million tokens.

A refusal mechanism trained on unanswerable examples taught the model to say it does not know at a measured rate. The system now runs at more than forty financial institutions. It improved query resolution by about seven points while answering several times faster and far cheaper than GPT-4.1.
arxiv-2605-05582:
A Grauert tube is a complex-geometric halo built around a real-analytic manifold, and whether entire tubes are affine has been open for decades. Kyobeom Song gives a partial answer to Burns' 1982 conjecture on the question. Affine spaces are the simplest Stein manifolds, so the answer probes how rigid these tubes are.

Song proves that removing a codimension-one subset from an entire Grauert tube leaves an affine space. The proof runs through a generalized version of Demailly's criterion for when a Stein manifold is affine. That generalized criterion, the paper notes, may be useful well beyond this conjecture.
arxiv-2605-05682:
Who attacks an AI system shapes what weaknesses get found. Wesley Hanwen Deng and seven co-authors build PersonaTeaming, bringing simulated personas into automated red-teaming. Automated attacks scale well but ignore the human identities that steer real probing; human red teams have the identities but not the scale.

Their workflow generates adversarial prompts through personas with distinct backgrounds and perspectives. The aim is a wider spectrum of attacks than generic automation produces. The project also studies how humans and persona-driven agents can collaborate, so each side covers the other's blind spots.
arxiv-2605-05882:
Parity rules demand predictions independent of protected traits, but sometimes a trait fairly shapes outcomes through approved middle steps. Filip Edström, Guilherme W. F. Barros, Tetiana Gorbach, and Xavier de Luna work on causal fairness rules that separate allowed from forbidden influence paths. Existing path-based rules cope mainly with grouped traits.

The authors use tuning derivatives to extend the framework, measuring how predictions shift along each causal route. Their approach pairs parity with predictive parity, asking the model to keep fair influence while cutting the rest. Continuous traits come within reach of the same analysis.
arxiv-2605-05982:
Harin Lee and five co-authors ask whether melody and rhythm evolve together across musical cultures. Music everywhere rests on these two parts, yet they might follow separate paths under different pressures. Testing that idea at scale used to need hand made annotations of songs from many traditions.

The team built a pipeline that extracts pitch intervals from vocals and timing patterns from percussion automatically. It covers 27,628 popular songs from 59 countries, and national similarities matched geographic and linguistic ties. Melodic and rhythmic diversity varied widely across countries but were not significantly linked to each other. Only rhythmic diversity tracked ethnic and linguistic diversity within countries, which suggests the two parts of music are shaped by partly separate forces.
arxiv-2605-06182:
Junjie Huang and Chang-An Zhao construct locally repairable codes with availability from elliptic function fields. Such codes protect data in large distributed cloud storage, letting a failed block be rebuilt from a small local set. Availability means more than one disjoint recovering set exists, so repairs can proceed even when some helpers are busy or down.

Earlier optimal constructions used maximal supersingular elliptic curves. The authors instead use ordinary elliptic curves with many rational points, which broadens the curves available for building optimal codes. Their families offer flexible locality at useful lengths. A general framework using automorphism groups of elliptic function fields yields codes with two recovering sets. One family reaches near optimal defect bounds at squared alphabet size, extending the known design space.
arxiv-2605-06282:
Brenda Bracco and thirteen co-authors test a basic assumption about silica films used in gravitational wave detector mirrors. Thermal noise in mirror coatings depends on the elastic traits of their materials, and analyses usually treat each material as uniform and direction independent. That isotropy had never been directly verified for ion beam sputtered silica, a leading candidate for future coatings, until this study.
